nodes.label: Deployment Procedure
nodes.rationale: The procedure companion to the roadmap's hosting section: written to be followed in order, from localhost to something members and staff actually use.

nodes.label: Four-Hostname Caddy Topology
nodes.rationale: my. and api. are public; outlet. and admin. are internal only. Four things run and three are static files. The API is public and has to be — members open the app from home, from a plane, from another country. What is restricted is not the backend but which routes answer which source addresses.

nodes.label: pgp_app / pgp_owner Role Separation
nodes.rationale: docker/postgres/init/01-app-role.sh only runs on first initialisation of an empty data directory. Point the API at a managed Postgres, connect as the owner because that is what the connection string came with, and redemption immutability disappears silently — no test fails, no error appears. A raw UPDATE smoke test must be run after every deploy that touches the database.

nodes.label: TRUST_PROXY Behind Caddy
nodes.rationale: Fastify sees the proxy's address unless told to read X-Forwarded-For. Leave it off and every per-IP rate-limit bucket collapses into one and every audited ipAddress records the proxy — both controls silently stop working while appearing present. Off by default, because a directly-exposed API must not believe the header or a caller picks their own bucket and forges their own audit trail.

nodes.label: INTERNAL_CIDR Staff Network Restriction
nodes.rationale: Must contain the staff/back-of-house VLAN and the VPN, never guest Wi-Fi merely because it is inside the building. A tablet on cellular is refused by design. /admin/* must be restricted on the public API host as well as the dashboard hostname, or the restriction is decorative. Defence in depth: source address reduces exposure and never becomes identity.

nodes.label: Outlet Device Token Provisioning
nodes.rationale: Admin -> Outlets issues one token per physical device; the API stores only its SHA-256 digest so the plaintext cannot be retrieved later. Rotate when a token may have been copied, revoke one-way when a device is lost. Never share one outlet-wide token: separate rows are what let a lost tablet be disabled without taking the other counters offline. Device labels become the outlet-level actor on immutable redemption history.

nodes.label: IDENTITY_CODE_HMAC_SECRET Rotation
nodes.rationale: Rotating it invalidates every printed card at once — which is also the only recovery a printed credential has. So the value must be in the secret manager and backed up before a print run, not generated casually at deploy time.

nodes.label: Google Sheets Mirror Deployment Prerequisites
nodes.rationale: Leave GOOGLE_SHEETS_SYNC_ENABLED=false until the hotel approves Workspace and data residency, a dedicated workbook exists with link sharing off, named administrators are Viewers and only the service account is Editor, and the private key is in the deployment secret store. Perform one manual reconciliation and confirm no member name, phone or email appears before enabling the schedule.

nodes.label: Nightly Encrypted Backups and Restore Drill
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL is the authoritative record and the Google Sheet must never be treated as a backup. Immutable redemptions and append-only audit logs protect against tampering and do nothing about a lost disk. An untested backup is not a backup — restore one into a scratch database before launch and again quarterly, with someone other than the script's author following the runbook.

nodes.label: Post-Deploy Verification Checklist
nodes.rationale: Not a checklist to skim — each item has failed silently in a real system. TLS on all four hosts, security headers, internal hosts refusing an outside address, CORS not answering a stranger, liveness and readiness distinguishable, R7 holding, and no member name in container logs.

nodes.label: Migrations as an Explicit Release Step
nodes.rationale: Never run migrations automatically on container boot: two containers starting together both running migrations is a bad afternoon. Seeding is for development; in production the first administrator is created by hand, once.

nodes.label: Camera Requires a Secure Context
nodes.rationale: getUserMedia refuses outside a secure context, so the outlet camera does not work over plain HTTP at all and there is no configuration that changes it. localhost counts and a LAN address does not, which makes TLS a prerequisite for testing a scan on a real counter tablet. Typing a membership number is the documented fallback.
